items.title: Louis Cottrell, Jr. Interview, 1961-08-25
items.q: Ralph arranged the interview... I saw Ralph over here when I worked that night

ctx.x: Are you watching the time, by the way? Do you have anything else that you have to run along to? We don't want to keep you doing this. No, I was just noticing. No, it's all right. Ralph arranged the interview and I didn't know just how long you had. No. I mean, he happened to see you. Really, really?

I saw Ralph over here when I worked that night and I came that Friday, but no one was here. Dick happened to be here. That's right. And no one was here. You had gone out. Dick was here a while. That's true. And so today when he came, well, I do know on Fridays is the only day that I do have a little time. That's true. So when I saw him there, I said, well, it's best today. I don't know when I'll have this time again. That's wonderful. We've been wanting to talk to him for a couple of years or so. Yes, I did. I…

Sure. Yeah, that's right. You know how commission, brother. That's right. And with your musical activities, and the officer, the president of the union is naturally one of the busiest men I can imagine. Yeah. Thank you. Let's see if we have a few more minutes. Well, can we go back to, we were talking about the C clarinet.
